candidate.title: HiTS-FLIP
candidate.scope: The middle row labeled HiTS-FLIP: flow-cell sequencing followed by duplex rebuilding, fluorescent protein binding and optical readout. The adjacent SELEX/SELEX-seq/HT-SELEX and DamID rows are separate catalogue context. The left Protein binding site icon describes the biological target, not an additional input branch. The cited Nutiu et al. implementation resolves the protein identity and the pre-scan interface; concentration-series affinity estimation and spatial sequence matching clarify the readout without adding a new assay target.

operations.mechanism: Cluster generation and sequencing by synthesis precede stripping of the second strand; internal library-preparation steps are not expanded.
operations.information_effect: DNA sequence identity is recorded at each cluster position before protein binding.

method_scopes.rationale: One target workflow. Operations o_prepare through o_scan retain the depicted route and captions. o_prescan uses the primary-supported pre-imaging interface while preserving the inconsistent poster label in c_prescan. o_associate explicitly identifies the paper-supported interpretation of the final image. The generalized schematic is supported by the Gcn4p implementation, without asserting that every HiTS-FLIP application uses that protein or the same target library.

corrections.diagram_observation: The HiTS-FLIP row labels a pre-scan step Elute with increasing stringency, shows a pale overlay beside a protein-bound duplex, and sends the surface directly to Scan flowcell. No collected eluate or new library is drawn.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper reports fluorescent-protein introduction followed by an optional wash and fluorescence imaging; binding is re-imaged at different protein concentrations to estimate affinity. Its supported interpretation of this interface is optional pre-imaging wash, not progressive-stringency elution as the source of affinity values. The operation and its output therefore use that primary-supported interpretation while retaining the poster caption.
